compiled_state.description:
## Problem
The completion verifier has exactly two verdict exits — PASS and FAIL — so every GATE PATHOLOGY (not a judgment that work is incomplete) is rendered as FAIL with unmet criteria. 7-day store mining (2026-08-07..14) shows this is the dominant availability cost: 7 ZERO-BANKING-WEDGE incidents (verifier banks nothing — proven budget-INDEPENDENT on cf3c: "4x budget: 97 search_files, 0 banks"), a provider fault (a3f3: Bedrock InvalidSignatureException after 625.7s → no verdict), an unitemized FAIL (2a6f run 3: "returned FAIL without itemizing the failing criterion"), and stale-snapshot false evidence (2a6f run 1: "claimed zero comments and status open while the store held 12 committed events"). Store-wide: 146 FORCE_CLOSE audit records vs only 4 confirmed false-METs ever — "the gate's operational cost is availability, not integrity" (dd41). Every pathology-as-FAIL steers operators to --force or attestation misuse.

## Fix: a retryable ERROR outcome, schema-enforced FAIL itemization
1. New verdict outcome `ERROR` (gate could not judge; retryable) alongside PASS/FAIL — NOT a softening of FAIL: judgment outcomes stay fail-closed; ERROR is reserved for detectable pathologies:
   - zero-banked exhaustion: search exhausted AND the bank holds zero records (the starvation oracle) — distinct from partial-bank exhaustion which stays FAIL with evidence_sufficient:false markers (1788 semantics);
   - provider/transport faults that today surface as no-verdict exceptions;
   - finalizer output failing schema validation (see 3).
2. Close-gate handling: ERROR never closes a ticket and never renders "unmet criteria"; the message states the pathology class + retry guidance; exit code distinct from FAIL (gate refusal) so automation can retry/re-verify without misreading refutation.
3. Schema enforcement: a FAIL verdict MUST itemize >=1 failing criterion in `criteria[]` (completion_verdict.schema.json conditional); a FAIL that cannot itemize is invalid and becomes ERROR — eliminating unitemized FAILs.
4. Stale-snapshot guard: before verdict production, assert the pinned ticket snapshot's event count/status matches the store HEAD read at run start; a mismatch is ERROR (stale snapshot), not evidence.
5. Signing: ERROR is never signed (no attestation minted), mirroring today's no-verdict path but typed and rendered honestly.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Zero-banked exhaustion produces ERROR (typed, unsigned, distinct exit code), never a FAIL naming unmet criteria; partial-bank exhaustion still produces FAIL with 1788 markers; RED->GREEN both.
- [ ] A provider/transport exception during verdict production surfaces as ERROR with the pathology class in the message; unit test with a faulting runner.
- [ ] Schema rejects FAIL with empty criteria[]; the reconcile path converts schema-invalid FAIL to ERROR; round-trip tests.
- [ ] A stale ticket snapshot (store HEAD advanced past the pin) is detected and yields ERROR, not false evidence; fixture test.
- [ ] Close-gate refusal on ERROR names the retry path and never suggests [operator-attested]; message test.
- [ ] `make lint`/`make typecheck` clean; lands via Gerrit (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
compiled_state.title: Completion verifier: retryable ERROR outcome for gate pathologies (zero-banking, provider faults, unitemized FAIL, stale snapshot)
